info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance · Unit 2 — Reading and signing off a task card. Items split by skill: listening, reading, use of English, vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. B asks which inspection lamp to select. Which lamp does A tell B to use?

generalfeedback.text: A says: "Use the borescope lamp, because the AMM note specifies a high-intensity light source." The choice comes from the AMM note, not from the mechanic's preference.

feedback.text: Correct — the AMM note specifies a high-intensity source.
No — a hand torch is not high-intensity enough for a weld check.
No — the dialogue does not mention an ultraviolet lamp.
No — the AMM note requires a directed high-intensity source.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Say whether this is true or false:

The mechanics refit the original lockwire that they removed.

generalfeedback.text: False. Step five is "fit new lockwire on the bolts, and never reuse the original wire." Used lockwire is work-hardened and can fail, so it is always discarded.

feedback.text: Correct — new lockwire is fitted and the old wire is discarded.
Not true — the card says never reuse the original wire.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. To how many newton metres are the two bolts torqued? (Enter the number only.)

generalfeedback.text: 25. A says "torque the two bolts to 25 newton metres", and B confirms the wrench "clicked twice, confirming the value".

feedback.text: Correct — 25 newton metres.
That is the avionics-unit value in Dialogue 3, not this job.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many fasteners secure the access panel? (Enter the number only.)

generalfeedback.text: 8. A warns "eight fasteners secure it", and B confirms "all eight fasteners are collected safely in the tray". Counting fasteners out is how you make sure none is left inside the aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct — eight fasteners.
Twelve is the flap-track card in the reading, not Dialogue 1.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. A finds a small crack in the hydraulic line. Where does B say the defect must be raised?

generalfeedback.text: B says: "Raise it in the tech log; afterwards we open a separate task card for the repair." The defect is recorded in the tech log, and the repair is a separate job.

feedback.text: Correct — the defect is raised in the tech log.
No — the work order authorises the job; the defect goes in the tech log.
No — the AMM is a reference manual, not a defect record.
No — that is a physical cover, not a document.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Say whether this is true or false:

A CAUTION box warns of a risk to a person.

generalfeedback.text: False. B explains a CAUTION "indicates a risk to the component". A WARNING protects people; a CAUTION protects the part; a NOTE is advice only.

feedback.text: Correct — a CAUTION protects the part; a WARNING protects people.
Not true — that describes a WARNING, not a CAUTION.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. To how many newton metres are the avionics-unit fasteners torqued? (Enter the number only.)

generalfeedback.text: 8. A says "torque the fasteners to 8 newton metres, following the specified cross pattern." The value is lower than the 25 Nm bracket job — each card gives its own value.

feedback.text: Correct — 8 newton metres, in a cross pattern.
25 is the bracket job in Dialogue 1, not the avionics unit.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Say whether this is true or false:

A functional test must be run before the access panel is closed.

generalfeedback.text: True. The NOTE says "a functional test is required before we close the access panel." B runs the built-in test and the screen reports no defect, so the unit is serviceable.

feedback.text: Correct — the NOTE requires the test before the panel is closed.
Not false — the NOTE clearly requires the test first.

questiontext.text: Listen to the shift-handover voicemail again. Under which tech-log reference number was the defect raised? (Enter the number only.)

generalfeedback.text: 4471. The late-shift lead says "I raised it in the tech log under reference number 4471, for traceability." A reference number lets the next shift find the open item.

feedback.text: Correct — reference number 4471.
12 is the stand number, not the tech-log reference.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL entry, then answer.

MEL item 25-11: One of the two cabin reading lights may be inoperative for up to 10 days, provided the light is deactivated and the switch is placarded "INOP".

For how long may the reading light stay inoperative under this MEL?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL (Minimum Equipment List) allows the item to be inoperative for up to 10 days, but only if it is deactivated and placarded. A relief is always conditional.

feedback.text: Correct — up to 10 days, if deactivated and placarded.
No — the entry states 10 days.
No — the relief is a fixed 10-day period.
No — misreading the number; it is 10 days.

questiontext.text:
Read this Airworthiness Directive, then answer.

AD 2024-07: Mandatory. Inspect the rudder hinge for cracks within the next 100 flight hours. Compliance is not optional.

Say whether this is true or false:

An operator may choose to ignore this Airworthiness Directive.

generalfeedback.text: False. An Airworthiness Directive (AD) is mandatory — it is issued by the regulator and compliance is required by law. A Service Bulletin may be recommended, but an AD must be done.

feedback.text: Correct — an AD is mandatory and cannot be ignored.
Not true — "mandatory" means compliance is required.

questiontext.text:
Read this IPC extract, then answer.

In the IPC (Illustrated Parts Catalogue), the bracket assembly is item 40 on figure 5. It comprises two bolts (item 45) and one lockwire kit (item 50).

Which item number is the lockwire kit?

generalfeedback.text: Item 50. The IPC lists each part with a figure and item number so you order the exact component. The bracket is 40, the bolts are 45, the lockwire kit is 50.

feedback.text: Correct — the lockwire kit is item 50.
No — item 40 is the whole bracket assembly.
No — item 45 is the two bolts.
No — item 55 is not listed in the extract.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order, then answer.

Work order WO-88231: Authorises the removal and replacement of the No. 2 static inverter. Refer to AMM 24-21-00 for the procedure.

Say whether this is true or false:

The work order lists each detailed step of the procedure.

generalfeedback.text: False. A work order authorises the job and points to the reference; the detailed steps live in the AMM procedure and on the task card. The two documents do different work.

feedback.text: Correct — it authorises the job and refers you to the AMM for the steps.
Not true — the steps are in the AMM, not on the work order.

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout, then answer.

FAULT 21-3 · AIR DATA MODULE · INTERMITTENT · LAST LEG · NO CURRENT FAULT

What does the readout say about the fault right now?

generalfeedback.text: The BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) shows the fault was intermittent on the last leg but reports NO CURRENT FAULT — so nothing is failing at this moment. An intermittent, non-current fault is monitored, not automatically replaced.

feedback.text: Correct — the readout ends "NO CURRENT FAULT".
No — the fault was intermittent, not a hard failure.
No — "NO CURRENT FAULT" means it is not active now.
No — an intermittent, non-current fault is monitored first.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the line as one task-card step. Use the imperative — start with the base verb.

"You must remove the access panel." → ______

generalfeedback.text: Remove the access panel. Drop the subject and the modal "must"; begin with the base verb and keep the article the.

feedback.text: Correct — base verb + the.
Correct.
Start with "Remove" and keep the article: "Remove the access panel."

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the line as one task-card step. It is a negative command.

"You must not touch the connector." → ______

generalfeedback.text: Do not touch the connector. A negative step uses "do not" + the base verb — not "not touch" and not "touch not".

feedback.text: Correct — do not + base verb.
Correct.
Correct — the contraction is fine in speech; a card writes it in full.
Use "Do not" before the base verb: "Do not touch the connector."

questiontext.text:
Write the one missing word.

"Torque ______ bolt to 25 newton metres."

generalfeedback.text: the. English needs the definite article before a specific, known noun. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so this word is often dropped.

feedback.text: Correct — the definite article.
The missing word is the article "the".

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the line as one task-card step.

"You should inspect the weld." → ______

generalfeedback.text: Inspect the weld. Drop the subject and "should"; a procedural step uses the bare verb with no modal.

feedback.text: Correct — bare imperative.
Correct.
Start with the base verb only: "Inspect the weld."

questiontext.text:
Write the one missing preposition.

"Inspect the bracket ______ cracks."

generalfeedback.text: for. The fixed collocation is "inspect (something) for (a fault)" — inspect for cracks, inspect for wear, inspect for damage.

feedback.text: Correct — inspect for cracks.
The collocation is "inspect for": you inspect a part for a fault.

questiontext.text:
Write the one missing preposition.

"Torque the fastener ______ 8 newton metres."

generalfeedback.text: to. You torque a fastener "to" a value — the preposition marks the target figure. Torque to 8 Nm, torque to 25 Nm.

feedback.text: Correct — torque to a value.
The collocation is "torque to": you torque a fastener to a value.

questiontext.text: Match each term with its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: task card = the list of steps for one job · AMM = the master reference manual · tech log = the book where defects are recorded · reference = the manual number the card points to.

correctfeedback.text: Correct — every term is matched to its meaning.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are right. Re-read the meanings and try the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: Check the pairs again — start with the documents you know best.

answer.text: the list of steps for one job
the book where defects are recorded
the manual number the card points to

questiontext.text: Match each action verb with the object it goes with on a task card.

generalfeedback.text: inspect → the bracket for cracks · torque → the bolt to a value · fit → new lockwire · remove → the access panel. Learning the verb with its object fixes the collocation.

correctfeedback.text: Correct — each verb is with its natural object.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some are right. Say each pair aloud as a step and try again.

incorrectfeedback.text: Check the pairs — think what you actually do to each object.

questiontext.text: Match each warning box with what it protects.

generalfeedback.text: WARNING → a person · CAUTION → the component · NOTE → nothing; it is only advice. If a person can be hurt, it is always a WARNING.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some are right. Remember: WARNING is always about a person.

incorrectfeedback.text: Check again — ask who or what is at risk.

answer.text: a fault found on a part

questiontext.text: Match each maintenance document with its purpose.

generalfeedback.text: work order → authorises the job · task card → lists the steps · Service Bulletin → recommends a modification · Airworthiness Directive → mandates a required action. Knowing which document does what tells you what is optional and what is law.

correctfeedback.text: Correct — each document matched to its job.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some are right. The AD is the mandatory one — start there.

incorrectfeedback.text: Check again — which one is required by law?
